messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: HyperNova inference eval — prioritizing interop tests and latency matrix

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion and useful context on the workload (short chatty responses, median token length ~45). Quick recap of the numbers we captured in the sandbox run and suggested next steps so we can turn this into a prioritized A/B test plan:

Key snapshot (sandbox run, 8xA100-equivalent):
- Redwood (default config): p95 = 135 ms, p99 = 320 ms, steady-state tokens/sec = ~3,900
- Hyperscale A (their managed endpoint): p95 = 180 ms, p99 = 560 ms, tokens/sec = ~2,600
- Hyperscale B (hot-path optimized): p95 = 150 ms, p99 = 400 ms, tokens/sec = ~3,200

Observations:
- Redwood shows consistent p95 advantage; p99 variance driven largely by cold KV-cache on long-tail requests
- Hyperscale A has higher tail latencies under bursty bursts in our probe
- Tokens/sec differences are sensitive to batching and sequence length distribution — we should align the synthetic generator to your real traffic (you mentioned 12% long-context bursts)

Proposed next tests (priority order):
1) A/B: Redwood -> Hyperscale A using your production request generator (same seed) measuring p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec across 1h steady-state windows
2) KV-cache warm vs cold probe: quantify p99 delta with 0%, 50%, 90% prefix cache hit rates
3) Batch-size sweep: batch sizes [1,4,8,16] at fixed concurrency to find cost/latency sweet spot
4) Quantization parity check: Redwood int8 path vs Hyperscale int8 variant (if available)

Ask from you: can you provide (or confirm) a representative traffic generator and a target SLO for p95/p99? From our side Jordan and Karthik will own bench orchestration and can run tests in your account if you prefer (or we can provide isolated infra).

Attaching a one-page snapshot and a proposed test matrix (csv) to make it actionable.

Next step: 30-min sync to finalize matrix and run window — are you available Wed morning PST?

Thanks,

— Soojin

Quick answers:
- We can provide the production request generator (we'll share a sanitized version by EOD Tuesday).
- Target SLO we'd like to aim for: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms for our 95% traffic; we accept higher tail for the long-context bursts but want quantifiable bounds.
- We prefer tests run from our cloud account (cloud-sales@hyperscale.com will open a temporary perf project) — security team will need firewall/ingress details.

One ask: can Redwood include the tokens/sec and cost-per-10k-tokens estimate for each configuration? That will help our procurement team. Also looping procurement lead Elena on timeline and docs.

Proposed test matrix (high-level) — I'll drop a fuller version in the Drive:

- Long-context burst: inject 1% synthetic long sequences (token length 512) every 3 minutes to measure tail amplification

All — thanks, this is a good plan. Small additions before we lock the window: 

1) Measurement guidance: please ensure the generator sends identical request ordering for A/B to avoid warmup bias. We'll run three 1-hour windows per vector and report median of medians.

2) Data retention & evidence: HyperNova security asked for audit logs and per-token breakdowns post-test — Marissa to set up a read-only export (48 hours retention for test artifacts).

3) Cost estimate cadence: we'll provide cost-per-10k-tokens for each vector within 24 hours of tests completing. If you want a pre-test estimate we can model it but it will be sample-based.

Proposed immediate milestones:
- Tue EOD: HyperNova shares sanitized generator + cloud project details (Samir)
- Wed AM: Redwood provisions perf project access & initial dashboard (Marissa)
- Wed 2pm PST: 30-min sync to finalize matrix and start first run (confirmation)

If Wed 2pm PST works for everyone I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the runs.

— Soojin
